ratings.comment: I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned in this class. Not only was the professor never available, but all of the material was so unclear, the entire class relied on each other for clarification.
Not the best professor in a virtual setting. It was hard to learn from lectures as they were pretty proof-based, not many example problems.

Abhishek is great lecturer. He teaches straight out of the textbook, but explains the material very well. The lectures are good for conceptual understanding. It would be great if he could post answer keys for the practice and actual exams.

I took Math 320 online and it was fine. Im sure it would have been pretty hard in person, though. Abhishek lectures straight from the textbook, word for word, so honestly, the lectures aren't super useful. He sends out practice exams before midterms that are super similar to the actual exam, which are super helpful.

Abhishek seems like a very smart guy. However, his lectures are straight from the textbook. I look forward to the beginning of his lectures as he always starts with "alright, let's get started" but after that the lectures are fairly confusing as the material doesn't really make sense. I took this class fully online.

His lectures consisted of proofs/theorems, and rarely involved actual examples of the concepts we were learning. Although his lectures were the least helpful way to learn, that was not the worst part about him. He refused to release keys for practice exams or past exams, so it was pointless to do the practice exams as you could not verify answers.

Took Calc with him last year. Had never taken a calc class before but listening to his lectures made the class easy. He was pretty easy to understand. However, I worked super hard in the class. My advice: Crush the first exam. I got like a 48 or 49 out of 50 points on the first exam and this carried me as the material got harder.

I have now taken both Math 211 and Math 141 with Professor Deshpande. He is about as dry of a professor as you can find. His lectures, while moderately helpful, are very long and hard to pay attention to. He never updated the gradebook the entire semester until posting the final grades. I would strongly advise against taking a class with him.

He only used textbook examples which made lectures close to useless. He never explained things clearly and didn't answer questions well. For a class that is an introduction to calculus, he made it extremely hard to learn and form a baseline as he didn't give any more examples or resources to find if you didn't grasp the content.

Final Remark: Sometimes Professors can get F's too. To describe Abishek in a nutshell he is a proof-based textbook teacher. In his lectures he covers basic examples of concepts, only to then give you insanely hard homework assignments that are nowhere near the same level. The only way to succeed is to get a good TA and make a study group right away

HE IS TERRIBLE!!! cannot understand him. LATE to his own class!!!!! wtf?! does not know how to work a microphone. i took AP calculus and did not attend a single lecture or discussion and did fine. claims he has a curve but sets higher grading standards than the university!!!!

Professor Deshpande really cares about his students. Those who complain about him most likely did not put in the effort to do as well in the class as they would have liked. Professors who are this smart are bound to make easy subjects seem harder than they are. Go to lecture and office hours and youll be fine!

Professor Deshpande taught the basics covered in the first exam very clearly. However from then on his lectures were confusing and towards the end he started teaching Calc 2 and Calc 3 concepts which should not be in a business calc class. Handwriting can be hard to read at times.

Professor Deshpande did a solid job at teaching this course. Taught straight out of the textbook, yet reading the textbook is a good idea if you want to see a few more examples and be more prepared. He was always accessible and helpful in office hours. Practice exam was VERY helpful for our first of 3 exams. Homework is the other 15% of grade.

Professor Deshpande does a pretty okay job at being a professor. He is pretty dry like mentioned in another post and I feel like even though he probably has a personality, he does not show it like ever. He focuses a lot on how to get to a formula when I just want to know what it is. Also, his handwriting is difficult to discern sometimes.

I preferred my high school calc teacher. I had heard that the calc teachers at Madison weren't great, but I never realized they were "nasty". I think the only reason I was ok in this class was because I already had a lot of knowledge in calculus (and it was still pretty tough). Hopefully he starts taking his critiques more seriously.

The lectures are extremely dry and he goes too fast. His handwriting can be difficult to read and his accent is a little confusing. The worst part is that 85% of your grade is based on tests. However, he does post practice exams that have a "similar flavor" to the actual exam; however no answer key is posted. Overall just OK.
He sucks

Abhishek "is this clear" Deshpande. If you take this guy for a math class, you'll hear this phrase around 25 times a lecture. Even this man's handwriting has an accent. You're better off watching a 10 minute youtube video than you are by attending a lecture.

Literally taught straight out of the book, even every single example he used in class. Claimed that it wasn't a proofs class, then put them on the exam. Asked the class questions, told you that you're wrong, then rephrased your answer as correct. Skip lecture, just read and do homework.

I really liked Prof. Deshpande's Math class. The material covered was pretty theoretical but he put a lot of effort in making it interesting and relatable. The homework and exams were just about the right level for us . He was also very caring and was always available available outside class for questions and guidance.

He is a nice guy but not good at teaching. There are lots of proofs in homework and exams. Textbook and TA can save you. If you do the homework seriously and understand every single question, then you can survive from this course. There's a curve because I only get 80% and also get an A... He thinks we are all smart, but unfortunately, we're not...

He was not horrible. The first test was difficult and no one knew what to expect from him. Once he got a better understanding of how to present the material, it got much easier. He likes to focus on proofs which is frustrating; however, he did base his exams off the homework which made studying for proofs and other problems much easier.

For students taking this course in future - The instructor is knowledgeable, patient, and takes care to make sure students in the class understand the concepts. If you put in work, the effort would be worth it. First exam was difficult and his lectures could be better organized, yet I feel I am much better at those concepts after taking this course
Stunningly Bad. Avoid at all costs.

I think university is not high school, so no one should expect spoon feeding. I found his knowledge reasonably high. He solved my doubts in office hours. His lectures were not organized as fall 2018 was his first experience of teaching.
Overall bad experience lacked knowledge on how to actually teach the class.

Every semester it seems like I've found the worst teacher at UW-Madison. But this guy was the worst. He really has no idea what he is doing. He also doesn't bother communicating with students most of the time. The entire course was proof based which made it very difficult and essentially useless.

It was his first semester here and I think his first semester teaching so I'm giving him a 2 solely on that. He will ask the class questions on new material and won't give up until someone answers. He does not understand that this isn't a proof-based course. Just wasted time and was not clear what the exams were going to be like. Avoid him.

He is a new professor who is obviously intelligent, but is severely out of touch with the level of explanation necessary in lecture and is often unorganized. Homework includes very few practical problems and instead has proofs that are impossible to solve without help. He is constantly improving with feedback so future years may be different

This was his first semester here and I'm not sure if this was his first time teaching but you could tell he would just teach from the book. Repeated himself a lot and very rarely used concrete examples. He was trying his best and he seems smart, you could tell he cared. No study guides. He is nice but this class matters so I wouldn't recommend him

Abishek was the worst professor I have had since I started at Madison. His first semester teaching was Fall 2018. He expects too much out of his students. Homework is challenging and is made up largely of proofs (need chegg or slader). First exam was very hard, second was easier. Take someone else if you can.
